skill.name: wp-playground
skill.description: Create and test temporary WordPress Playground environments in a browser or local CLI, using blueprints for plugins, themes, snapshots, and demos.
skill.summary: Launch disposable WordPress Playground sites for plugin tests, theme previews, WooCommerce demos, and blueprint workflows.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting or official WordPress Playground documentation URLs, and the hidden ~/.claude path is a false positive. Confirmed risks are expected but meaningful: npx CLI execution, WordPress plugin/theme installation, PHP or WP-CLI blueprint steps, remote blueprint loading, and broad local directory mounting.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the Playground CLI version, ask for user confirmation before running commands, and recommend disposable workspaces for CLI tests.

remediation.issue: Remote blueprint URLs can execute setup steps
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to load only trusted blueprint URLs and to review runPHP, wp-cli, writeFile, installPlugin, and installTheme steps first.

remediation.issue: Directory mounting can expose local files
remediation.suggestion: Advise mounting only a minimal plugin or theme directory and avoiding project roots that contain secrets or private data.

remediation.issue: Networked plugin and theme installs are expected but implicit
remediation.suggestion: Document that WordPress.org plugins and themes are downloaded and activated during blueprint setup.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Blueprint Trust Warning Missing
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows loading a remote blueprint URL while documenting blueprint steps that can run PHP, run WP-CLI, and write files. Users need an explicit warning to review remote blueprints before use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The remote blueprint URL example is clear, and the same file lists powerful blueprint steps. The issue is missing trust guidance, not hidden malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Local Directory Mounting Warning Missing
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends auto-mounting the current directory and mounting local plugin or theme paths without warning users to avoid secrets or broad project roots.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mount commands and auto-mount workflow are explicit. The risk depends on the working directory contents, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: WordPress testing often needs a fast site without Docker or hosting. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Playground URLs, blueprints, CLI usage, and demos.
actual_capabilities: Open the official WordPress Playground URL for instant test sites.
Create blueprint-based sites with selected plugins, themes, versions, and site options.
Run local Playground CLI sessions with custom ports, PHP versions, and WordPress versions.
Mount local plugin or theme directories for preview testing.
Build and reuse Playground snapshots for demos.
Use the JavaScript API pattern for embedded Playground control.
limitations: Playground data is temporary unless exported or saved as a snapshot.
Performance is slower than native PHP or Docker.
Networking, cron, email, and WP-CLI support are limited.
Remote blueprints and npm commands should be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Run Plugin Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Create a disposable site, install a plugin, test key screens, and close the environment after review.

use_cases.title: Prepare WooCommerce Demos
use_cases.description: Start a temporary store with WooCommerce, Storefront, SEO tooling, and basic store settings.

use_cases.title: Preview Theme Changes
use_cases.description: Mount a local theme folder and inspect changes in a browser without a full server stack.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Clean Test Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-playground skill to start a basic WordPress Playground site. Choose browser access unless I ask for CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Plugin Test Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WordPress Playground blueprint plan for testing [plugin slug]. Include versions, login behavior, plugins, and site options.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a WooCommerce Demo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WooCommerce blueprint pattern to plan a temporary store demo. Include plugins, theme choice, store settings, and demo steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Playground Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Playground command or blueprint before I run it: [paste details]. Identify network access, mounted paths, and unsafe steps.

output_examples.input: Create a temporary site for plugin testing.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with selected versions, required plugins, launch method, test steps, and cleanup notes.
A demo checklist covering store settings, theme choice, required extensions, sample content, and sharing approach.

output_examples.input: Review a Playground command before running it.
output_examples.output: A risk summary that flags npm execution, mounted folders, remote blueprints, and safer alternatives.

best_practices: Review every blueprint before running it, especially runPHP, wp-cli, writeFile, and remote blueprint URLs.
Use a minimal test directory when mounting local code.
Pin WordPress, PHP, plugin, and CLI versions when reproducing bugs.
anti_patterns: Do not load remote blueprints from sources you do not trust.
Do not auto-mount a project root that contains secrets or private data.
Do not treat Playground performance or email behavior as production-equivalent.

faq.question: Does this skill require Docker?
faq.answer: No. WordPress Playground runs in a browser or through the Playground CLI without a Docker stack.

faq.question: Can it test WooCommerce?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a WooCommerce blueprint pattern with WooCommerce, Storefront, SEO tooling, and store settings.

faq.question: Does it run local commands?
faq.answer: It can guide CLI commands that use npx. Review each command before running it.

faq.question: Will site data persist?
faq.answer: Not by default. Export a snapshot or use a saved environment when you need repeatable state.

faq.question: Can it use local plugin or theme files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI examples mount local directories, so use a limited folder without secrets.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production sites?
faq.answer: No. Use it for testing, demos, and temporary previews, not production hosting.
